record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.context_brief: Infinite complex spectrum for smaller γ
record.original_question: For dimensions d≥2, decide whether there exist bounded complex potentials V in L^(γ+d/2)(R^d) for every γ>1/2 such that the non-selfadjoint operator −Δ+V has infinitely many eigenvalues in the lower half-plane accumulating at every point of [0,∞).

evidence.quote: Whether such V exist even for γ > 1/2 in d ≥ 2 is open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 2$ and let $-\Delta$ denote the Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For a (possibly complex-valued) potential $V\in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^{\gamma+d/2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, consider the closed non-self-adjoint Schrödinger operator $H=-\Delta+V$ acting in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, defined on the domain of $-\Delta$. Its essential spectrum equals $[0,\infty)$, and its discrete spectrum consists of isolated eigenvalues of finite algebraic multiplicity in $\mathbb{C}\setminus[0,\infty)$.

Determine, for every $\gamma>1/2$, whether there exists a bounded complex-valued potential $V\in L^{\gamma+d/2}(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that the operator $-\Delta+V$ has infinitely many eigenvalues in the open lower half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Im} z<0\}$ which accumulate at every point of $[0,\infty)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Bögli and Štampach (Schrödinger Operators with Complex Sparse Potentials, Comm. Math. Phys. 2022; arXiv:2102.12706) constructed, for every $q>(d+1)/2$, a complex potential $V\in L^q(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that the discrete eigenvalues of $-\Delta+V$ accumulate at every point of $[0,\infty)$. Since $q=\gamma+d/2>(d+1)/2$ is equivalent to $\gamma>1/2$, this answers the question affirmatively for all $\gamma>1/2$ in every dimension $d\ge 2$.

status_evidence.title: Schrödinger Operators with Complex Sparse Potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative version of Bögli's example; for q>(d+1)/2 there is a complex V in L^q∩L^∞ whose Schrödinger operator has eigenvalues accumulating at every point of the essential spectrum [0,∞).
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative answer to the existence question for all γ>1/2 in d≥2.

status_evidence.title: Schrödinger Operator with Non-Zero Accumulation Points of Complex Eigenvalues (Bögli, CMP 2017)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs V∈L^p∩L^∞ with p>d such that -Δ+V has infinitely many non-real eigenvalues accumulating at every point of [0,∞).
status_evidence.claim: Earlier weaker result requiring p>d, i.e. γ>d/2; the γ>1/2 range remained open until 2022.
